## context.md — live project context (context-md)

This repo is wired to **context-md**. Rules for EVERY AI agent, no exceptions:

1. **BEFORE doing anything**, read `context.md` at the repo root. It holds the live
   project snapshot, structure, agreed purpose, key knowledge, current focus and a
   timestamped change log.
2. **AFTER any meaningful decision or change**, update `context.md` in place:
   - *Purpose* — what this project is, once you know it.
   - *Key Knowledge* — stack/architecture decisions, conventions, gotchas.
   - *Current Focus / Next Steps* — what is being worked on right now.
3. Never delete the `context-md:*` markers or the auto-managed sections. Edit only
   the agent-owned sections by hand; hooks maintain the rest.
4. If `context.md` is missing, run `node .context/hooks/session-start.js` or
   `npx context-md refresh` to regenerate it, then read it.
5. **Strict gates (agent-dependent):** on Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI /
   Cursor, hooks BLOCK edits until context.md is read, and BLOCK turn end
   until context.md is updated. On opencode and agents without turn-end
   hooks, the rule is the same but enforced by you: read first, update always.
6. `context.md` is meant to be committed — it is the shared brain of the team.

Hooks installed by context-md keep a change log on every file edit and refresh the
snapshot at session start. The file can drift between sessions — re-read it; do not
trust your memory over it.

# context-md

**Live `context.md` for AI agents.**

## What it is / how it works

Your repository carries one live file — **`context.md`** — containing the
complete, always-current description of your project: what it is, how it is
built, the decisions already made, the current focus, and a timestamped change
log of everything that happened in it. Install it once (`npx agent-context-md
install`) and every AI agent you use reads that file first. From then on,
every hook-capable agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor; opencode via
a plugin) is wired with five local mechanisms: **(1)** on session start the
hook refreshes `context.md` and injects "MANDATORY: read this first" into the
agent, **(2)** the agent cannot edit any file until it has read `context.md`
this session (the edit tool is hard-denied), **(3)** every file edit is
appended to the change log in real time, **(4)** ending the turn/session is
blocked while an edit was made without `context.md` being updated, and **(5)**
CI can fail on stale context (`context-md verify`). Instruction files cover
20+ agents (Copilot, Windsurf, Devin, Continue, Junie, Amazon Q, Cline, Roo,
Kilo, Augment, Tabnine, Zed, Aider…), all hooks run locally with **no API
keys, no server, no telemetry** — and you get the whole thing out of the box
by installing once.

## The problem

Every new AI coding session starts with amnesia: the agent re-derives your
stack, re-learns conventions, forgets yesterday's decisions, and its context
window compacts away whatever it eventually figured out. Teams lose hours per
week re-explaining their own project to machines.

Existing answer candidates (`CLAUDE.md` by hand, Cline Memory Bank, heavy
frameworks like `skill-memory-bank`, MCP memory servers, repo packing) all
either put the burden on you, only support a subset of agents, or require
servers/Python/bash. None of them *enforce* a single live file every agent
must respect.

## What this does

```bash
npx agent-context-md install      # in any repo, or in every project on your machine
```

After install:

1. **Before any work**, the agent reads `context.md` at the repo root — what
   the project is, its structure, decisions, current focus, change log.
2. **Every file edit** is appended to that file's Change Log — real-time.
3. **Every prompt** steers the agent toward the live file (Claude/Codex/Gemini).
4. **Editing is hard-blocked** until `context.md` has been read this session.
5. **Ending the turn/session is hard-blocked** while files changed without
   `context.md` being updated (Claude/Codex/Gemini/Cursor).
6. **CI can fail** when `context.md` is stale (`context-md verify`).

If the repo was never backfilled, the agent gets a one-time deep pass: read
README/manifests/key sources, run `git log --oneline -50`, and rewrite
`context.md` Purpose + Key Knowledge with real project facts.

## Quick start

### Per repository (share with your team)

```bash
npx agent-context-md install          # interactive: pick your agents (TTY)
npx agent-context-md install --all    # wire all supported agents
npx agent-context-md install --clients claude-code,codex,gemini-cli   # pick by id
cd your-repo && context-md verify .   # CI freshness check
```

`context.md` is created with snapshot + structure + an agent-maintained
knowledge section; commit it so teammates (and their agents) get full context
for free.

### Globally, on your machine (every project, zero setup)

```bash
npx agent-context-md install --global        # one time
# or pick specific agents:
npx agent-context-md install --global --clients claude-code,gemini-cli
```

Creates a standalone `~/.context-md/` runtime and wires your user-level agent
configs (`~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.codex/hooks.json`, `~/.gemini/settings.json`,
`~/.cursor/hooks.json`, global opencode plugin). From then on, **every
project-like folder you open with these agents gets `context.md` automatically** —
no per-repo step. The global runtime only activates in folders containing
`.git` or a known manifest, defers to a repo's local wiring when present,
and is fully reversible with `context-md uninstall --global`.

### What you will see

```
context-md: detecting agents on this machine…
  [1] Claude Code    (command on PATH, config ~/.claude seen)
  [2] Codex (OpenAI) (config ~/.codex seen)
  ...
Enter = all detected, numbers "1,3" = pick, "a" = all, "n" = none
```

(Selection only controls **hook adapters**. Instruction files are installed for
every supported agent regardless.)

```

  CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md ...  ← same protocol, one per agent convention
  .clinerules                ← Cline
  .github/copilot-instructions.md
  .kiro/steering/context-md.md
  .cursor/rules/context-md.mdc
  .devin/rules/context-md.md / .windsurf/rules/context-md.md
  .continue/rules/context-md.md   (Continue)
  .junie/guidelines.md            (JetBrains Junie)
  .amazonq/rules/context-md.md    (Amazon Q)
  .roo/rules/context-md.md        (Roo Code)
  .kilocode/rules/context-md.md   (Kilo Code)
  .augment/rules/context-md.md    (Augment)
  .tabnine/guidelines/context-md.md
  .rules / CONVENTIONS.md         (Zed / Aider)
  .context/                     ← the runtime the hooks call (commit it)
    hooks/session-start.js      ← fires on session start: refresh + brief the agent
    hooks/read-gate.js          ← fires pre-tool: deny edits until context.md is read
    hooks/prompt-gate.js        ← fires per prompt: strict protocol injection
    hooks/post-tool.js          ← fires on every edit: change-log + snapshot refresh
    hooks/stop-check.js         ← fires on turn end: block if context.md not updated
    lib/scan.js, lib/context-file.js
    package.json                ← {"type":"module"} so hooks always parse
  .claude/settings.json         ← hook wiring (backed up as *.bak-<ts>)
  .codex/hooks.json
  .gemini/settings.json
  .cursor/hooks.json
  .opencode/plugins/context-md.js
```

Per-session runtime state (`.context/session-state.json`, `.context/.last-scan`,
`*.bak-*` backups) is auto-gitignored by the installer; `.context/` itself is
meant to be committed.

## The `context.md` file, section by section

```markdown
# context.md — live project context
> Maintained by context-md — every agent MUST read it; hooks maintain it.

## Snapshot                        ← auto-managed (between markers)
- Updated: 2026-11-18T15:06:53Z
- Git: main @ 501286e · 3 uncommitted changes
- Stack: Node.js + TypeScript · Next.js · pnpm
- Files (excl. deps/build): 132 · dependencies: 47
- Scripts: dev=`next dev`, test=`node --test`

## Structure                       ← auto-managed (between markers)
src/  (42 files)
test/ (6 files)
package.json ...

## Purpose                         ← agent-owned
(what this project IS — the agent writes this once it understands the repo)

## Key Knowledge                   ← agent-owned
Stack & architecture: decisions, patterns, constraints
Conventions: naming, testing, commit style
Gotchas: things that would bite a newcomer

## Current Focus / Next Steps      ← agent-owned
(what is being worked on RIGHT NOW, and what comes next)

## Change Log                      ← auto-managed (between markers)
- 2026-11-18T10:29:08Z context.md created
- 2026-11-18T11:02:51Z edited "src/index.ts"
- ...
```

**Auto-managed sections** (Snapshot / Structure / Change Log) are rewritten by
hooks and must never be hand-edited — they are regenerated from the repo state.
**Agent-owned sections** (Purpose / Key Knowledge / Current Focus) are yours
(and the agent's) to keep current; the stop gate makes sure they are.

If `context.md` loses its markers (hand-edit gone wrong), the session-start
hook does NOT delete it — it moves the broken file aside as
`context.md.broken-<timestamp>` and starts fresh, preserving your data.

## Why there are no API keys

context-md is **not** an LLM. It ships no model, no server, no phone-home, no
telemetry. The only processes are the hook scripts your agent invokes; they
read the repo, write `context.md`, print JSON for the agent. Your subscription,
your models, your data — untouched.

## How the real-time update works (the honest version)

| Layer | What happens |
|---|---|
| Session open | Hook refreshes Snapshot/Structure, injects "MANDATORY: read context.md first" + backfill protocol if needed |
| Every user prompt | Strict protocol reminder injected (Claude/Codex/Gemini) |
| Before any edit | **Read gate**: file edits are *denied* until context.md was read this session |
| After every edit | One line appended to Change Log; snapshot refreshed when stack manifests change |
| End of turn | **Stop gate**: turn is blocked while an edit was made without updating context.md (max 2 re-blocks, then releases) |
| CI | `context-md verify` fails the build when files changed without a context.md refresh |

No tool can make an LLM retain everything it never writes down. What context-md
guarantees: nothing is *silently* lost — every edit is logged, reading is
enforced before editing, and ending a turn without syncing is blocked on hook-capable
agents. What an agent still cannot do for you is remember a decision it never
wrote; that's why the backfill pass exists.

## Commands

```bash
context-md install [dir] [--all] [--clients a,b]   # wire a repo
context-md install --global [--all] [--clients a,b] # machine-wide default
context-md uninstall [dir]                          # remove wiring (keeps context.md)
context-md uninstall --global                        # remove machine-wide wiring
context-md uninstall --remove-context [dir]          # also delete context.md
context-md backfill [dir]                            # regenerate + print the backfill protocol
context-md refresh [dir]                             # rebuild snapshot/structure now
context-md verify [dir]                              # CI check, exits 1 when stale
context-md doctor [dir]                              # health check (all green = ready)
context-md status [dir]                              # what is wired (repo + global)
context-md --help | --version
```

`verify` prints `OK: context.md is fresh` or `STALE: … Run context-md refresh.`
`doctor` prints PASS/FAIL per check and exits non-zero on any failure.

### CI example (GitHub Actions)

```yaml
name: test
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npx agent-context-md install --all .   # wire in CI (optional)
      - run: npx agent-context-md verify .
```

## Uninstall (clean, provable)

```bash
context-md uninstall .              # removes blocks + hook wiring, KEEPS context.md
context-md uninstall --remove-context .
context-md uninstall --global
```

Removes only what context-md created: marked blocks in instruction files
(restored), context-md hook entries (other hooks you wrote are preserved),
`.context/`, and for `--global` the `~/.context-md` runtime and global hook
entries. Config files are backed up before every edit (`*.bak-<timestamp>`);
back up your config if you want to double-check with `git diff`.

## Troubleshooting

- **Codex does not fire hooks** — Codex requires trust review: open `/hooks`,
  review and trust the context-md entries.
- **Gemini hooks seem ignored** — Gemini fingerprints project hooks; changed
  hooks need re-review. SessionStart output uses scaffolding; context.md is the
  source of truth regardless.
- **User's settings "went away"** — they didn't: invalid/BOM-prefixed JSON is
  never overwritten (the adapter skips that agent with an error). Look for
  `*.bak-<timestamp>` next to the file.
- **"context.md has broken markers"** after a hand-edit — session start moves
  the broken file to `context.md.broken-<timestamp>` and rebuilds; your content
  is preserved there.
- **Install reports `invalid JSON — not touched`** — the config file exists but
  is corrupt/non-standard. Fix it or remove it, then re-run.
- **Everything looks fine but `verify` fails** — files changed after
  `context.md`; run `context-md refresh`, then commit context.md.

## Security

Committed `.context/` is executable code that every clone runs when an agent
opens the repo — treat it like CI workflow changes in review. The installer
never overwrites an existing (possibly hand-edited) `context.md`, refuses to
write through symlinks, and leaves unrelated config untouched. See
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the threat model, safe use, and reporting.

## FAQ

**Does the agent see `context.md` if its IDE is closed?** The hooks only run
while the agent runs — but the committed `context.md` is always on disk; the
next session re-injects it.

**Do teammates need to install?** No — if you commit `context.md` and
`.context/`, any teammate with a supported agent gets the wiring for free on
their next session.

**Does it cost money?** No. Zero API keys, zero servers, zero telemetry.

**Does it work on Windows?** Yes — tested on Windows 11 (PowerShell, Git Bash)
with Claude/Codex/Gemini/Cursor paths. The hook commands are
machine-independent and committed with relative/env-var paths
(`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`, `./.context/hooks/…`, `$GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR/…`,
`$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/…`).

**Can I use only one agent?** Yes: `--clients claude-code` (or any subset),
or pick interactively.

**What if I don't want it in a repo?** Don't commit `.context/` there — or
remove the wiring with `context-md uninstall`.

# Changelog

## 0.1.0 — 2026-11-18

First release. npm package name: **agent-context-md** (the `context-md` CLI
command is unchanged; `npx agent-context-md install` works out of the box).

### Added
- `context-md install [dir]`: wires a repository — creates `context.md`, injects the
  context protocol into `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`,
  `.cursor/rules/context-md.mdc`, `.kiro/steering/context-md.md`, `.clinerules`,
  `.devin/rules/context-md.md`, `.windsurf/rules/context-md.md`, and wires hooks into
  Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`), Codex (`.codex/hooks.json`), Gemini CLI
  (`.gemini/settings.json`), Cursor (`.cursor/hooks.json`) and opencode
  (`.opencode/plugins/context-md.js`).
- **Live hooks**: `SessionStart` refreshes `context.md` and tells the agent to read it
  first; `PostToolUse` appends every file edit to a timestamped Change Log and
  tracks per-session edits in `.context/session-state.json`.
- **Stop gate**: `Stop` hook (Claude Code / Codex), `AfterAgent` deny→retry
  (Gemini CLI), `stop` hook with followup (Cursor) — blocks turn end until
  `context.md` was updated after the last edit.
- **Read gate**: pre-tool hook hard-denies file edits until `context.md` has
  been read this session (Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI / Cursor).
- **Strict prompt injection**: `UserPromptSubmit` / `BeforeAgent` hook injects
  the non-negotiable protocol into every prompt (Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI).
- **Auto-create**: a missing `context.md` is recreated on the first tool call
  and at session start — fresh projects can never skip it.
- **`context-md doctor`**: verifies context.md markers, hook files and agent
  configs; exits non-zero on any problem.
- **PUBLISHING.md**: maintainer release + live-verification playbook.
- **Security hardening** (review-driven): symlink-safe, atomic writes everywhere
  (tmp + rename); corrupt agent configs are skipped, never overwritten; unexpected
  `hooks` shapes are left untouched; `git status -z` quote-safe freshness check;
  persistent per-session stop-gate block counter (max 2 then let the turn end);
  read gate clears only on an actual read of the file (read-ish tool or shell
  read verb), never on `echo context.md`; uninstall never deletes
  `~/.opencode/plugins/context-md.js`; git-ignored `*.bak-*` patterns for every
  config the tool backs up; `--home=`/`--home <dir>` both supported with
  directory validation.
- **First-run backfill**: repos wired for the first time get a one-time deep
  backfill — the agent must read README/manifests/key sources and rewrite
  `context.md` Purpose + Key Knowledge with real facts (`.context/.backfill-done`
  marks completion; the stop gate enforces it after any edit).
- `context-md install --global`: machine-wide default — a standalone `~/.context-md`
  runtime + user-level agent hooks, so every project you open gets `context.md`
  automatically (project-like folders only; defers to locally wired repos).
- `context-md verify [dir]`: CI freshness check (fails if files changed but
  `context.md` was not refreshed).
- `context-md backfill [dir]`, `refresh`, `status`, `uninstall` (repo + `--global`),
  BOM-safe JSON merging, idempotent marked-block installs, backups before config writes.
- Machine-independent, committable local hook commands (`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`,
  `$GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR`, `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`, `./.context/...`).
- 23 end-to-end tests (`node --test`), GitHub Actions CI on Node 18/20/22.
- Explicit limitation notes: opencode has no verified turn-end hook; Windsurf/Cline
  stop gates untested; hooks are best-effort and never block file edits.

## Purpose

Zero-dependency Node CLI (`context-md`) that wires **any repository** to live `context.md` maintenance. Every AI agent that opens the repo reads one shared context file before working; hooks keep a real-time change log after every edit, and a stop gate blocks session end until `context.md` was updated. Distributed via GitHub (`npx github:<user>/context-md install`), MIT, Node >= 18.

## Key Knowledge

- Two runtime layouts, ONE codebase: repo-local `<repo>/.context/` (committed, team-shared) and machine-wide `~/.context-md/` (global default, activates only in project-like folders, defers to local wiring to avoid double logging). Hooks detect layout via `path.basename(path.resolve(__dirname, '..'))` (`.context` vs `.context-md`).
- Hook templates in `src/templates.js` are ONE template string per hook — raw backticks or `${}` inside them break compilation. Paths in hook commands are always forward-slash; local installs emit machine-independent, committable commands (`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`, `$GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR`, `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`, `./.context/...`); global installs keep absolute paths.
- JSON merge must strip UTF-8 BOM (`readJson`) — Windows tools write BOM-prefixed configs or the user's existing settings silently vanish (backed up as `*.bak-<ts>` regardless).
- Install is idempotent: instruction files use `<!-- context-md:start/end -->` markers; hook groups are deduplicated by keeping the last entry containing `.context/hooks/` or `.context-md/hooks/` (HOOK_TAGS in src/install.js).
- Agents with turn-end hooks get a hard stop gate (Claude `Stop`, Codex `Stop`, Gemini `AfterAgent` deny→retry, Cursor `stop` followup + loop_limit 2). Editing any non-context file sets `pendingEdit: true` in `.context/session-state.json`; only a later context.md edit clears it. `backfillPending` forces a one-time deep backfill per project.
- `context.md` is split into auto-managed marked sections (`context-md:snapshot|structure|log:start/end`) maintained by hooks and agent-owned sections (Purpose / Key Knowledge / Current Focus). Never hand-edit the marked sections.
- Tests are end-to-end `node:test` against temp git repos; the global-mode tests use `--home` to simulate a user machine (`install --global --home <tmp>`).
- Not published to npm yet; installation is `npx github:…` or local `node bin/context-md.js install`.

  swallow errors, print only valid JSON (strict hooks like Gemini parse stdout).

## 1. Pre-flight

```bash
npm test                  # 23/23 must pass

```

CI (.github/workflows/test.yml) runs the same tests on Node 18/20/22 on every push.

## 2. Push to GitHub

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/BilalAjmad/agent-context-md.git
git push -u origin main
```

## 3a. GitHub-only release (no npm account needed)

Users install with:

```bash
npx github:<YOUR_USER>/context-md install
npx github:<YOUR_USER>/context-md install --global   # machine-wide default
```

## 3b. npm publish (optional, cleanest `npx agent-context-md` UX)

```bash
npm login
npm publish               # MIT, public, files: bin + src

```

## 4. Verify live (once agents have credits)

```bash
mkdir /tmp/ctx-live-test && cd /tmp/ctx-live-test && git init -b main
echo '{"name":"ctx-live-test"}' > package.json && git add -A && git commit -m init
npx github:<YOUR_USER>/context-md install .
claude -p "Create hello.txt containing 'hello'" --permission-mode acceptEdits
cat context.md                # template + fresh doctor pass
npx github:<YOUR_USER>/context-md doctor
```

Expected: the first `Edit` is denied by the read gate; the agent reads
`context.md`; the edit lands; the stop gate forces a `context.md` update;
`context-md doctor` reports all green.

## 5. Post-publish checklist

- [ ] Tag `v0.1.0` and push the tag; create a GitHub Release from CHANGELOG.md.
- [ ] README badges (optional): CI status.
- [ ] Monitor issues for hook-format drift in agent updates (Cursor `1.x` hook
      APIs and Gemini `BeforeAgent` are the fastest-moving surfaces).

## Troubleshooting

- **Codex hooks don't fire** → Codex requires trust review: open `/hooks`, review
  and trust the context-md entries, or restart Codex.
- **"API 402 / insufficient credits"** when live-testing → that is the model
  account's credits, not the tool; hooks can only be verified at their
  stdin/stdout contract level without a working model account.
- **Windows BOM** — all config edits backed up as `*.bak-<timestamp>`; restore
  those if anything looks wrong, then re-run `context-md install .` (idempotent).

# Security

context-md installs hooks into your repositories and, optionally, your user-level
agent configs. Please read this before using it — the tool **executes code the
next time a supported agent opens the wired repo**.

## Threat model

**What context-md is.** A file walker, a file writer, and a hook runner. It:

- writes `context.md` and keeps it fresh (agent-owned + hook-owned sections),
- injects marked instruction blocks into agent config files (AGENTS.md, …),
- copies a small JS runtime into `<repo>/.context/` and points agent hook
  configs at it,
- optionally (`--global`) writes a standalone runtime at `~/.context-md/` and
  hooks it into your user-level agent configs.

**Executable code you commit.** When you commit `.context/` (the normal flow),
every clone of the repo executes those hook files with your user privileges
whenever a supported agent starts a session, hits a tool call, submits a prompt,
or ends a turn. **Treat `.context/` diffs in pull requests exactly like CI
workflow changes.** A compromised PR that edits `.context/hooks/*.js` is remote
code execution on every contributor's machine.

**Generated configs point at `node "<abs path>" …` (global) or
`node "./.context/hooks/…"` (local).** Local commands are machine-independent and
safe to commit; global commands embed your home directory path and are kept out
of version control.

**context.md is data, not instructions.** The file may contain paths and text
sourced from your repo and tools (branch names, file paths, script names). An
agent reading it must not treat its content as directives. The injected protocol
tells agents exactly that.

## What the tool guarantees

- Zero runtime dependencies, no network calls, no telemetry, no postinstall.
- Writes refuse symlinks (`lstat` check) and are atomic (tmp file + rename).
- Your JSON configs are backed up as `*.bak-<timestamp>` before any change, and
  BOM-prefixed configs are handled on both read and write.
- If an agent config exists but is unreadable/invalid JSON, the adapter **skips
  that agent** instead of overwriting your file.
- If your `hooks` object contains an unexpected shape (non-array value) for one
  of our managed events, the adapter leaves it untouched and reports an error.
- Uninstall removes only hook entries that point at `.context/hooks/` or
  `.context-md/hooks/` (backed up first), the runtime, our instruction blocks
  and the repo's `.context/` — never anything else. `context.md` is kept unless
  you pass `--remove-context`.
- Global mode only activates in project-like folders (containing `.git` or a
  known manifest) and defers to a repo's local wiring when present.

## What it cannot protect you from (honest limits)

- **Agent decisions.** The gates (read gate, stop gate) are advisory deny-lists,
  not a sandbox. A malicious or careless agent can ignore its instruction file,
  and hooks cannot force an LLM to remember anything it refuses to persist.
- **A repo that ships hostile hooks before you install.** Inspect `.context/`
  after first opening an untrusted repo — it is yours to audit, not ours.
- **`--global` blast radius.** User-level wiring applies to every project you
  open, including ones you never intended to wire. Use
  `context-md uninstall --global` to undo.
- **Backup files** (`*.bak-<timestamp>`) contain your pre-edit agent configs,
  which may include MCP server URLs, absolute paths, or API keys if you stored
  them there. They are gitignored in wired repos but must not be committed —
  delete them when you are satisfied with the result.
- Races in `.context/session-state.json` (read-modify-write with no lock) —
  gates may occasionally misfire under heavy parallelism; they are designed to
  fail best-effort, never to destroy data.

## Safe use

1. Run `npx github:<owner>/context-md install` only in repos you trust.
2. Review the diff before committing `.context/`.
3. Review any agent-config diff it produces.
4. Never point `--home` at anything but a real user home directory.
5. In CI, use `context-md verify` as a freshness check, never as a security
  boundary.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please do **not** open a public issue. Once the project is public, use GitHub's
private vulnerability reporting ("Report a vulnerability" in the Security tab).
Until then, open a minimal issue titled `security contact requested` and the
maintainer will arrange a private channel. Include the file, the trigger, and a
minimal reproduction; do not include secrets.

Supported versions: the latest release only.
